newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi to open euro show with Santer.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to open euro show with Santer.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will open an exhibition on Europe's planned new single currency in Rome next week with European Commission President Jacques Santer, the Treasury said on Wednesday.
A Treasury statement said the exhibition, called "Building Europe Together, from the lira to the euro" would open next Wednesday for three weeks.

The exhibition will form part of celebrations in the Italian capital next week to mark the 40th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Rome, which founded the six-nation European Economic Community (EEC).

Prodi and his centre-left government say they will do whatever is necessary to ensure Italy's finances are in shape for first wave membership of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999.

The government is due to unveil a supplementary budget within the next few weeks to try to achieve a 1997 deficit target of three percent of Gross Domestic Product, a key condition for first round entry into the currency union.
Some European politicians, however, have expressed doubts that Italy will be able to meet the criteria.
